subject: MAP: cost assumptions, eval plan & close dates for PulseNovo POC
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rios <alex@pulsenovo.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2024-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP kickoff: cost assumptions we need to lock for the POC

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time earlier. To keep momentum toward the June close window you mentioned, I put together a short list of MAP items we need to agree on so we can finalize procurement and spin up the dedicated POC capacity. High level ask: can you review the bullets below and confirm by end of week?

What we need from PulseNovo:
- Traffic profile: avg calls/day, expected peak parallel sessions, and percent of calls that are long-context (>2k tokens).
- Target SLOs: p95 latency target and acceptable per-request response length.
- Minimum committed tokens (monthly) for discount tiers.

Our assumptions (please flag anything off):
- Tokens per interaction: 350 prompt / 150 generation = 500 tokens average.
- Caching/prefix reuse: assume 25% of requests hit prefix cache (reduces prompt tokens).
- Effective batching expected: median batch size 6 for async routes, 1.5 for sync; improves throughput, lowers tokens/$ by ~8-12%.
- Baseline tokens/$ we will model for the MAP: $0.0009 per token for inference (model-dependent) before committed discounts.

Attached: draft MAP spreadsheet (PulseNovo_MAP_draft_v1.xlsx) and an eval prompt set (eval_prompt_set_v2.jsonl) that we want to use for regression checks.

Next steps: If those assumptions look reasonable I will loop in Karthik and Ben to validate the caching/batching knobs and produce an updated token/$ sensitivity table we can include in the SOW.

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

From: Alex Rios <alex@pulsenovo.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: PulseNovo Procurement <procurement@pulsenovo.com>
Date: 2024-06-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: cost assumptions we need to lock for the POC

Hi Soojin —

Thanks — looks good overall. A couple quick clarifications from our side:
- Traffic profile: estimate 12k calls/day, peak concurrency ~60, and maybe 8% long-context.
- Target SLO: p95 < 400ms for short responses (<=256 tokens); for long responses we can tolerate up to 1.2s.
- Commit: procurement prefers a 6-month committed token tier, but we need the financials to show the delta vs month-to-month.

Procurement asked that any MAP cost table include both a conservative and aggressive usage scenario. Also—can you confirm whether the caching assumption is applied pre- or post-token counting for billing? That materially changes our forecast.

Appreciate the docs, will review attachments this afternoon.

Alex
Director of Product, PulseNovo
alex@pulsenovo.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rios <alex@pulsenovo.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2024-06-22T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: cost assumptions we need to lock for the POC

Alex — thanks, that traffic profile helps. Quick answers up front:
- Caching and billing: Redwood bills on consumed inference tokens. If prefix cache avoids re-sending prompt tokens to the model runtime, those prompt tokens are not billed for that request; our conservative model assumes the cache reduces billed prompt tokens by the cache-hit percent. We will document the methodology in the MAP.
- We'll include conservative/aggressive scenarios (conservative uses 10% cache, aggressive 35% cache; conservative batching values lower).

Internal note to Karthik + Ben: can you do a quick pass on the attached MAP spreadsheet and add a tab with the sensitivity table (tokens/$ at 3 committed tiers, and an example monthly P&L at projected usage)? We want to send a single sheet to procurement that shows: monthly cost w/o commit, 3-month commit uplift, 6-month commit uplift, and expected unit cost under our recommended config (quantized model + batching + 25% prefix cache).

Alex — I'll turn that around in 24 hours and include a short explanation for procurement on how billing interacts with caching.

Thanks,
Soojin

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Alex Rios <alex@pulsenovo.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2024-06-23T13:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: cost assumptions we need to lock for the POC

Alex / Soojin — adding technical detail so procurement has confidence in the numbers. I kept it short:

1) Token assumptions per request (example):
- Prompt tokens: median 350; response tokens: median 150 => 500 total.
- If prefix cache hits, only response tokens are billed (so 150) + a small routing overhead (~5 tokens).

2) Batching effects:
- For async endpoints we expect batching to increase effective throughput and reduce wall time cost. In our sims: batch=6 => ~10% lower tokens/$ for the same throughput vs batch=1.
- For sync routes where latency is critical, batching is limited; use tail-latency-aware batching (max wait 25ms). Expect median batch~1.5.

3) Quantization / model variant:
- Using the 4-bit quantized variant yields ~15-30% cost reduction per token with minimal quality regression on our eval set. We'll include both full-precision and quantized lines in the sensitivity tab.

4) Billing note: our billing is by consumed model tokens after any cache elimination. We will add an example line showing billed tokens under conservative (10% cache) and aggressive (35% cache) scenarios.

I attached a quick csv in the draft MAP sheet with the sim numbers. If you want, Ben can produce a monthly projection table for the three commit tiers.

-karthik
Principal Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Rios <alex@pulsenovo.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, PulseNovo Procurement <procurement@pulsenovo.com>
Date: 2024-06-25T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: cost assumptions we need to lock for the POC

Soojin / Karthik — this is exactly the level of detail procurement wanted. Confirming next steps:
- We will review the MAP sheet and expected monthly token consumption; procurement will request a 6-month committed quote if numbers look favorable.
- Proposed close: target signature by 2024-07-05 to keep the POC start in mid-July.
- One ask: can Redwood include an illustrative discount scenario for a 6-month commit (volume bands) vs standard month-to-month pricing? That is the primary procurement gating question.

If you can attach the sensitivity table and the short 1-page methodology note for billing+caching, procurement will schedule a final review on 2024-06-27.

Thanks — Alex

PulseNovo Procurement contact looped in.
